reasoning: I keep the Market Analyst's risk-off stance (SPY 1.93% under its 200-day, 21d -6.88%, VIXY 5d +14.12%; data as of 11-25). The regime filter allows only BND, GLD, IEF and TLT. BND and IEF are wash-sale blocked, TLT is at its stated ~8% target (L4: no fourth add on the hedge week already counted), and the Market Analyst says gold is falling with stocks. No buy was proposed, so the roughly 53% cash after today is idled by the filter, not by choice, and it is no reason to keep any invalidated position. I approve P2, the one-third DPZ trim. The 11-24 and 11-25 runs accepted that DPZ was too large and only moved the stop, and L8 says that is not an answer. I accept the Skeptic's L4 point that a third was not sized toward a stated target, so I state one now: no single stock above about 8% of equity. A one-third trim lands at about 8.1% (Implicator), which meets that target. DPZ stays the largest stock, with its own $335 stop and no adds. I also accept the Skeptic's objection that 'beats SPY' grades a 0.117-beta name in a falling tape almost mechanically, so I restate the trim's test as an absolute-gain test. I reject P1, the full SAM sale. The Skeptic's case is stronger here, and the Fundamentals Analyst says SAM's fundamentals 'are fine and are not the case against it'. Every SAM-specific reason is missing information: the 8-K 5.02 closed unread and the CEO handover has been known since 11-19. Staples is the Market Analyst's first favored sector and it is leading (XLP 21d +5.91%, 9.43% above its 200-day). Selling would put the whole Staples tilt on KR four trading days before KR's company-confirmed 12-03 call, and it would turn about $15 of favored-sector exposure into cash the filter will not let us redeploy. The small loss would also start a wash-sale block that could bind if the filter turns back on. This answers L8's named-candidate check with a hold verdict that does not rest on beta, which SAM's stored thesis calls an artifact. SAM stays a sell candidate if Staples loses its lead, and I add that as a relative XLP-vs-SPY clause (L10). L7 clause check, every holding taken from its stop block (stop_alerts empty, all ok): CARG, IDXX, INCY, MSCI and VRSN have no guidance cut or negative 8-K (VRSN's 11-25 insider sale is a Form 4), and INCY has no failed pivotal trial. DPZ is on the menu with CFO $792M above net income $602M and no confirmed guidance cut. KR's cyber clause is unconfirmed and its guidance clause is untested until 12-03. SAM has no 2.02/7.01 guidance cut and is on the menu. TLT's relative clause is unmet (SPY 5d -1.85% vs TLT +2.52%), and so is its trend clause (0.41% under its 200-day, inside 4%). No stored clause is met and none tripped against its intent. All earnings dates come from the News Analyst's filings check (L2): KR 12-03 is the only held-name print in the window. L3: DPZ is counted by bucket (Consumer Discretionary), not by its Staples SIC label. KR and SAM remain one Staples factor bet at about 8.3% of equity. L9: no shared stop is held. L6: I fix VRSN's open text items (the reference to a guidance raise its thesis no longer states, and the stale 'top-ranked' claim). I also restate DPZ without a position-size claim and SAM without the owed-verdict line, since today answers it.

trades.thesis: Size trim, not a thesis break. No DPZ clause is met: it is on the menu, CFO is above net income, and there is no confirmed guidance cut. But at about 12% of equity it was the largest position, and two prior runs accepted that it was too large without changing its size (L8). The trim works toward a stated target of no single stock above about 8% of equity (L4). The remainder keeps DPZ's low-beta, cash-backed quality exposure with its own $335 stop. The lot is short-term until 2027-10-21, so there is no tax reason to wait. The realized short-term gain is about $3.
trades.invalidation: The trim is wrong if, over the next 20 sessions, DPZ's own return is positive and above SPY's, meaning the trimmed concentration would have paid in absolute terms (a mere relative beat in a falling market from a 0.117-beta name does not count).

rejected.why: The Skeptic is right that every SAM-specific reason is missing information rather than bad news, and the Fundamentals Analyst says the fundamentals are not the case against it. Staples is the Market Analyst's first favored sector and leading (XLP 21d +5.91%, 9.43% above its 200-day). The sale would put the whole Staples tilt on KR four trading days before its 12-03 print and turn the exposure into cash the regime filter cannot redeploy, while the wash-sale block could bind if the filter turns back on. The Implicator finds no tax reason either way. I hold SAM on the sector lead, not on its artifact beta, and add a relative XLP-vs-SPY clause that makes it a sale if that lead ends.

Its top-of-sector rank is partly an artifact of the wholesale-groceries SIC mislabel (bucket Consumer Discretionary), so the case rests on absolute quality and low beta, not on the Staples tilt. It fails leverage_not_up. Trimmed by a third on 11-27 for concentration. The single-stock target set that day is no more than about 8% of equity, so no adds. The only lot opened 2026-10-20 and is short-term until 2027-10-21, so there is no tax reason to hold. Sentiment items, not 8-K events: EVP and Chief Restaurant Officer stock sale (11-23) and BNP Paribas Underperform initiation with a $295 PT (11-24). Next earnings 2027-02-22 (file estimate).
